description: RANDOM([seed]) returns a signed 64-bit integer and a constant seed is deterministic; UNIFORM(min, max, gen) returns an integer INCLUSIVE of both bounds when the bounds are integers, or a double in [min, max) with a float bound, and a per-row RANDOM() varies it while a constant RANDOM(seed) repeats it across rows. Snowflake's UNIFORM is strictly three-argument, so UNIFORM(5, 10) is refused. The assertions check these invariants rather than specific draws. Converted 1:1 from functions/RandomUniformTest (now retired); its 50-row Java-built fixture becomes an INSERT ... SELECT over GENERATOR, the per-row range loops become COUNT_IF checks, the repeat-across-rows loop becomes COUNT(DISTINCT), and the instanceof Long / Double checks become TYPEOF(TO_VARIANT(...)) reading INTEGER or DOUBLE. Two tests keep the class's live exemptions.

steps.sql: INSERT INTO t SELECT SEQ4() FROM TABLE(GENERATOR(ROWCOUNT => 50))
SELECT TYPEOF(TO_VARIANT(UNIFORM(1, 3, RANDOM()))) FROM t LIMIT 1
SELECT COUNT_IF(r < 1 OR r > 3) FROM (SELECT UNIFORM(1, 3, RANDOM()) AS r FROM t)

skip.reason: asserts the runtime type of a single nondeterministic draw; over JDBC a live UNIFORM(0.0, 1.0, ...) arrives as a scaled decimal, and whether the upper bound is open is an RNG-internal detail of the account

steps.sql: SELECT r >= 0.0 AND r < 1.0 FROM (SELECT UNIFORM(0.0, 1.0, RANDOM()) AS r)
INSERT INTO t SELECT SEQ4() FROM TABLE(GENERATOR(ROWCOUNT => 50))
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT r) FROM (SELECT UNIFORM(1, 100, RANDOM(7)) AS r FROM t)
INSERT INTO t SELECT SEQ4() FROM TABLE(GENERATOR(ROWCOUNT => 50))
SELECT UNIFORM(5, 10) AS r FROM t
SELECT COUNT_IF(r < 5 OR r > 10) FROM (SELECT UNIFORM(5, 10, RANDOM()) AS r FROM t)
